name: es32-tessellation-domains
title: Tessellation domains, spacings and winding
summary: The fixed-function tessellation primitive generator: triangle, quad and isoline domains with equal / fractional odd / fractional even spacing, cw/ccw and point_mode, driven by a TCS that writes gl_TessLevelOuter/Inner, per-patch outputs and uses gl_InvocationID and barrier(). The TES output is captured with transform feedback and compared with a CPU implementation of ES 3.2 section 11.2.2 (exact for equal_spacing, structure and counts for fractional spacings), plus the program queries, patch-size rules, level clamping and discarding, and the defined errors. A 3x3 gallery of bumped, wireframed patches shows the result.
spec: ES 3.2 §10.1.12 Separate Patches (PatchParameteri PATCH_VERTICES, patch size initially 3, trailing vertices ignored, INVALID_VALUE range)

ES 3.2 §11.2 Tessellation (errors: PATCHES with and without an active tessellation program), §11.2.1 Tessellation Control Shaders (output patch size, per-patch outputs, gl_InvocationID, barrier ordering), §11.2.2 Tessellation Primitive Generation with Figures 11.1-11.4 (discarding, clamping and rounding of levels, equal / fractional spacing, cw / ccw, point_mode) and §11.2.2.1 / §11.2.2.2 / §11.2.2.3 (triangle, quad, isoline subdivision), §11.2.3 Tessellation Evaluation Shaders (gl_TessCoord, gl_TessLevel*, gl_PatchVerticesIn, gl_PrimitiveID)
ES 3.2 §7.12 Shader, Program, and Program Pipeline Queries (TESS_CONTROL_OUTPUT_VERTICES, TESS_GEN_MODE / SPACING / VERTEX_ORDER / POINT_MODE and their INVALID_OPERATION errors)

ES 3.2 §12.1 The Last Vertex Processing Stage, §12.2.2 Transform Feedback Primitive Capture and Table 12.1 (the tessellation primitive type decides the legal BeginTransformFeedback mode), §12.3 Primitive Queries (PRIMITIVES_GENERATED, TRANSFORM_FEEDBACK_PRIMITIVES_WRITTEN)

ES 3.2 §13.1 Discarding Primitives Before Rasterization (RASTERIZER_DISCARD for the captures), §13.5 Points (point size is 1.0 unless the last vertex processing stage is a vertex shader), §13.7.1 Basic Polygon Rasterization (FrontFace / CullFace with the generated winding), Tables 21.45 / 21.46 (MAX_TESS_GEN_LEVEL >= 64, MAX_PATCH_VERTICES >= 32)

GLSL ES 3.20 §4.4.1 Input Layout Qualifiers (Tessellation Evaluation Inputs: primitive mode, vertex spacing, ordering, point_mode and their defaults), §4.4.2 Output Layout Qualifiers (Tessellation Control Outputs: vertices = N), §4.3.4 / §4.3.6 (patch in / patch out), §7.1.2 and §7.1.3 Tessellation Control / Evaluation Shader Special Variables (gl_TessCoord obeys x == 1.0 - (1.0 - x)), §8.15 Shader Invocation Control Functions (barrier)

api.glPatchParameteri: PATCH_VERTICES 3, 4, 5 and MAX_PATCH_VERTICES give TCS gl_PatchVerticesIn (captured per vertex) and the number of patches of a PATCHES draw, trailing vertices that do not fill a patch are ignored; 0, -1 and MAX_PATCH_VERTICES + 1 -> INVALID_VALUE and the patch size stays unchanged
api.glDrawArrays: mode PATCHES: transform-feedback counts and gl_TessCoord sets equal the CPU model, the gallery pixels match; TRIANGLES / POINTS with a tessellation program and PATCHES without one -> INVALID_OPERATION; PATCHES while transform feedback has a mismatching primitive mode -> INVALID_OPERATION
api.glCreateProgram: tessellation programs (VS + TCS + TES [+ GS] + FS) are created and linked for dozens of layout variants, all of which run
api.glAttachShader: TessControl, TessEvaluation and Geometry shaders attach to the same program as vertex and fragment shaders; the programs run
api.glLinkProgram: links with the TCS output patch size from 3 up to MAX_PATCH_VERTICES; layout(vertices = MAX_PATCH_VERTICES + 1), vertices = 0 and a TES without a primitive mode do not link
api.glGetProgramiv: TESS_CONTROL_OUTPUT_VERTICES, TESS_GEN_MODE, TESS_GEN_SPACING, TESS_GEN_VERTEX_ORDER, TESS_GEN_POINT_MODE compared with the layout of 19 programs (defaults equal_spacing / ccw included); the same queries on a program without tessellation shaders -> INVALID_OPERATION
api.glTransformFeedbackVaryings: captures the TES outputs (gl_TessCoord, levels, patch outputs, gl_Position) that all CPU comparisons read
api.glBeginTransformFeedback: TRIANGLES for triangles/quads, LINES for isolines, POINTS for point_mode work; the wrong mode makes the draw raise INVALID_OPERATION (Table 12.1)
api.glEndTransformFeedback: ends every capture; the records are read back
api.glBindBufferBase: TRANSFORM_FEEDBACK_BUFFER binding of the capture buffer
api.glBeginQuery: PRIMITIVES_GENERATED and TRANSFORM_FEEDBACK_PRIMITIVES_WRITTEN run together and equal the CPU triangle / line / point counts
api.glEndQuery: ends both queries of every capture
api.glGetQueryObjectuiv: the two primitive counts compared with the CPU model (0 for discarded patches)
api.glMapBufferRange: reads the captured TES output for the CPU comparison
api.glGetIntegerv: MAX_TESS_GEN_LEVEL (>= 64) and MAX_PATCH_VERTICES (>= 32) from which the clamping rules and the largest patch are derived and verified
api.glUniform4f: gl_TessLevelOuter of the TCS: changing it changes the captured vertex and triangle counts as the CPU predicts
api.glUniform2f: gl_TessLevelInner of the TCS, same verification
api.glUniform1f: per-gl_PrimitiveID level bias (3 patches in one draw get levels 1, 2, 3), dome height and radius of the TES
api.glUniformMatrix4fv: model-view-projection: captured gl_Position equals the CPU projection of the CPU-evaluated TES position; gallery dots land on CPU-projected pixels
api.glFrontFace: with CULL_FACE(BACK), the generated cw / ccw winding is drawn or culled in all four combinations
api.glCullFace: BACK culls exactly the triangles whose generated winding is opposite to FrontFace
api.glEnable: CULL_FACE: with it enabled the generated cw / ccw triangles are drawn or culled as the cull probe predicts
api.glBufferData: the patch vertex buffers (3, 4, 5 and MAX_PATCH_VERTICES vertices per patch) reach the TCS/TES: captured gl_Position and centroids match the CPU
api.glVertexAttribPointer: position and tag attributes of the patch vertices (tag of vertex 0 captured in the TES)
api.glReadPixels: gallery probes: dot pixels at CPU-projected vertices, orientation colours, isolines, culling probe

visual_review.notes: 256x256 radeonsi capture viewed (llvmpipe and zink identical in structure): a 3x3 gallery of bump-shaped patches on a dark blue background. Row 1 triangles (teal, teal-front ccw / orange cw / teal), row 2 quads (orange cw / teal ccw / orange cw), row 3 isolines (four green lines over a faint dome). Every generated vertex is a white dot; wireframe lines visible; in the fractional columns the dots bunch toward the middle of the edges, as fractional spacing prescribes, while the equal column has evenly spaced dots. A 768x768 render confirmed the structure and the 3D shading.
